jobs.title: Behavioral Health Specialist (Assessment), Social Work/Counselor III - Youth Services Center
jobs.description:
**Department Information**
--------------------------

  

  

  

  

**This position will be accepting applications from residents and non\-residents of Colorado. This announcement is open to potential candidates who are legal residents of the United States. All legal residents of the United States are eligible to apply and compete.**  

**If appointed to a position, applicants from outside of Colorado will be required to relocate to Colorado prior to their start date, at their own expense.**  

Please note: This recruitment may be used to fill multiple vacancies.

 **Division of Youth Services \- Campus at Lookout Mountain** **Youth Services Center**

 **About the Division of Youth Services:** The Division of Youth Services (DYS) provides a continuum of residential and non\-residential services that encompass juvenile detention, commitment, and parole. DYS is the agency statutorily mandated to provide for the care and supervision of youth committed by the District Court to the custody of the Colorado Department of Human Services. The Division operates fifteen secure facilities that serve youth between the ages of 10 and 21, who are pre\-adjudicated, sentenced, or committed. The Division also contracts with numerous private residential and non\-residential service providers throughout the State. For pre\-adjudicated youth, the Division is also responsible for the management and oversight of Colorado Youth Detention Continuum, a State\-funded, locally administered program that provides services to youth at risk of further progressing into the juvenile justice system. In addition to residential programming, the Division administers juvenile parole services throughout the State.  

  

We invite you to explore the DYS website and learn about the services provided to youth, families, and local communities in the State of Colorado at: https://www.colorado.gov/cdhs/dys  


**Description of Job**
----------------------


You are required to work at your assigned work location during your scheduled work times. *Please note: Work arrangements are subject to change at any time.* **Summary of Work Unit:**  

It is the mission of the Division of Youth Services (DYS) to effectively build skills and competencies of youth to become responsible citizens. The Social Work series and other identified Behavioral Health Specialists employed by the facility are responsible for providing evidenced based and research supported therapeutic intervention services to youth committed and detained with the Division of Youth Services. Behavioral Health Specialists are expected to provide for the therapeutic care of and support opportunities for growth and change for youth and their caregivers, to ensure healthy and successful reintegration back into our communities. These positions maintain and support the DYS treatment model and Sanctuary principles with transition staff, client management, mental health services, medical, special education, security staff and administration as needed. As a Behavioral Health Specialist within our facility, they are expected to remain current on literature and research in the field, especially as relates to emerging practices with complex mental health populations and behavioral and sensory interventions.  

  

**Summary of the position:**  

The purpose of this position is to administer and interpret criminogenic, mental health, trauma, and substance abuse screening and assessment tools, in order to arrive at accurate and effective recommendations for placement and treatment goals for juveniles who have been committed to the Department of Human Services, Division of Youth Services. A primary aim of this position is to work within a multidisciplinary team to offer empirically supported criminogenic, mental health, trauma, and substance abuse evaluation services to the youth and families that DYS serves. This job class requires advanced educational degree, training, and experience in the discipline areas of criminal risk, mental health, trauma, and substance abuse screening and evaluation. This position conducts individual and family structured clinical interviews, administers and interprets psychological assessment information, acts as a liaison with psychiatric professionals, completes substance abuse screening and assessments, and participates as a team member and clinical consultant with other assessment and regional personnel. Information gained through the assessment process is synthesized into a comprehensive and professional report and is completed within the timelines specified in Colorado Revised Statues and internal implementing procedures.  

  

Conduct clinical interviews, criminogenic risk assessments, drug and alcohol screening and assessments, mental health evaluations, trauma assessment, and neuropsychological screenings on juvenile offenders who are committed to the Department of Human Services, Division of Youth Services. Administration and interpretation of the Colorado Youth Assessment Screening Instrument, Juvenile Automated Substance Abuse Evaluation (JASAE), and University of California Los Angeles Post Traumatic Stress Disorder – Reaction Index (UCLA PTSD\-RI) to assess specified areas of functioning including, but not limited to: current and past delinquent behaviors, mental health presentation, criminogenic need areas, family issues, peer relationships, self perceptions, use of free time, level of maturity, problem solving skills, breadth of decision\-making, drug and alcohol involvement, personal goals, risk factors associated with neuropsychological deficits, and identified skills/competencies. Conduct family interview to ascertain individualized family strengths, needs, perspective, and expressed goals for treatment and DYS stay. Outline the assessment process to youth and families, including expectations, responding to questions, and requesting signed authorization for release of information and disclosure statements.

jobs.title: Peer Support Specialist
jobs.description:
About the Role

Sagebrush Recovery is seeking a motivated **Peer Support Professional or Qualified Behavioral Health Assistant (QBHA)** to support justice\-involved adults in the Denver area through **Job Readiness and Health/Fitness programming**.

This is a strong part\-time opportunity for someone who is independent, organized, dependable, and skilled at building meaningful relationships with clients.

Unlike starting from scratch, this role comes with **established programming and an existing participant base**, providing a strong starting point for someone interested in developing a consistent caseload. Long\-term success will depend heavily on motivation, relationship building, client engagement, follow\-through, organization, and time management.

Current Program Opportunities

Sagebrush currently has established DOC/community corrections programming during the following times:

* **Wednesday: 1:00–3:00 PM**
* **Thursday: 1:00–6:00 PM**
* **Friday: 7:00–9:00 PM**
* **Saturday: 9:00–11:00 AM**

We are especially interested in candidates whose availability overlaps with these existing opportunities.

Additional opportunities for **individual client support and caseload growth** are available outside of established group programming.

What You’ll Do

* Facilitate **Job Readiness** programming for DOC/community corrections participants
* Facilitate **health, wellness, fitness, and healthy\-lifestyle programming**
* Provide individual peer and/or behavioral health support as appropriate
* Help clients develop employment readiness, life skills, healthy routines, accountability, and community stability
* Build strong relationships with clients while maintaining appropriate professional boundaries
* Encourage continued participation and engagement in available services
* Connect clients with employment, vocational, community, and re\-entry resources when appropriate
* Coordinate with Sagebrush leadership, facility staff, and other members of the client’s support team
* Complete timely and accurate documentation in accordance with Sagebrush, BHA, and Medicaid requirements
* Independently manage scheduling, client follow\-up, documentation, and communication

Minimum Qualification Pathways

Applicants must meet **at least ONE** of the following qualification pathways:

**A. Peer Professional Working Toward CPFS**

* Minimum of **60 hours of COPA\-approved peer support training**
* Currently working toward obtaining the **Colorado Peer and Family Specialist (CPFS) credential**

**B. Credentialed Peer Professional**

* Current **Colorado Peer and Family Specialist (CPFS) credential**

**C. Qualified Behavioral Health Assistant**

* Current **Qualified Behavioral Health Assistant (QBHA) credential**
* Minimum of **60 hours of accredited behavioral health\-related education or training**, which may include peer support training or relevant college coursework/training
* Minimum of **one year of experience in the behavioral health field in a client\-facing role**

Additional Requirements

All applicants must also have:

* High School Diploma or GED
* Valid driver's license
* Reliable personal vehicle and transportation
* Reliable computer or laptop for documentation and communication
* Strong organizational and time\-management skills
* Ability to work independently, take initiative, and consistently follow through
* Ability to complete required criminal background screening and meet applicable DOC/community corrections facility requirements
* Demonstrated stability and responsible community living for at least the previous two years

Preferred Experience

We **strongly prefer** candidates with experience in one or more of the following areas:

* **Job readiness, employment support, vocational services, or workforce development**, including resumes, applications, interviewing, job searches, workplace skills, and connecting individuals with employment resources
* **Fitness, exercise, wellness, sports, coaching, or healthy\-lifestyle programming**
* Working with **justice\-involved individuals, re\-entry populations, or individuals transitioning from incarceration**
* Knowledge of **Denver\-area employment, workforce, community, and re\-entry resources**

Candidates who bring a combination of **peer or behavioral health experience, employment\-resource knowledge, and an interest or background in health and fitness** will be especially strong fits for this role.

Justice\-System Lived Experience

**Previous incarceration, DOC involvement, probation/parole, or other lived experience within the criminal justice system is not a disqualifier and may be a significant strength in this role.**

Qualified applicants with personal experience navigating incarceration, re\-entry, supervision, or the criminal justice system are **strongly encouraged to apply**.

We are looking for individuals who are currently living stable lives, have demonstrated stability over the previous two years, and are able to meet applicable facility access and background requirements.

**Lived experience with substance use or recovery is not required for this position.**

Compensation

This is a **1099 independent contractor position with expected earnings of approximately $500–$1,000 per week**, depending on services provided, client participation, and overall engagement.

Sagebrush already has **established DOC programming and active participants**, giving the person entering this role a strong starting point rather than requiring them to build a caseload entirely from the ground up.

There are also opportunities to increase service volume through **individual client support and continued caseload development**.

Because compensation varies with actual client engagement, this role is best suited for someone who is proactive, dependable, comfortable building relationships, and motivated to maintain consistent client participation.

The full compensation structure will be reviewed during the interview process.
